title: Fruits Basket
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Orphaned high schooler Tohru Honda, living in a tent after her mother's death, is taken in by classmates Yuki, Kyo and their cousin Shigure of the Sohma family. Thirteen Sohmas are possessed by the spirits of the Chinese zodiac and turn into animals when stressed or hugged by the opposite sex. Tohru's kindness helps heal the family's wounds as she learns how deeply the curse, and its cruel head Akito, have harmed them, and sets out to break it.
life_message: It holds up compassion that accepts people as they are, and the courage to break inherited cycles of pain.

delivery.note: Compassion is shown through Tohru's relationships, and the abusive head of the family is drawn as a victim of the same system.

winners_losers: Compassion and the will to break inherited harm win; the clan's coercive order loses. Even its abuser, Akito, is given sympathy as a victim of the same system.
